conclusion: **Quality-coverage did not beat the published methods.** None of its exploratory Wilcoxon comparisons against the four published oversamplers, the re-implemented CLLM-style and discriminator-realism curators, or the existing selectors reached even nominal p < 0.05 (smallest p = 0.06), and its dataset-level differences were small and mixed in sign. Among the eight curators it had the best average rank only for logistic-regression F1 (3.75 of 8), and the Friedman tests found no consistent separation among curators (p = 0.21 to 0.65). Across all sixteen methods on the five datasets where every method ran, full-balancing SMOTE-Tomek and ADASYN ranked best for random-forest F1 (average ranks 3.7 and 4.5 against 7.6 for quality-coverage; Friedman p = 0.03, exploratory), mainly through large gains on yeast4 and ecoli1, while the same full-balancing oversamplers often lowered logistic-regression F1 (for example 0.63 to 0.68 against 0.78 on yeast3). Several published methods could not run everywhere: Borderline-SMOTE and ADASYN have no nominal-feature path, SMOTE-ENN and SMOTE-Tomek failed on nominal columns, ADASYN +b generated no samples on page-blocks0, and no curator could run on vehicle0. Our AUROC values are much higher than those in Newaz and Haq and the sign of the SMOTE effect matched theirs in only 5 of 12 dataset-classifier pairs, which is consistent with their different protocol (10-fold cross-validation, and an unsampled Abalone19 AUC of exactly 50.0 that suggests hard-label scoring), so this check is context rather than validation.
label: Exploratory addendum, declared after the main study.
